title: Social attention and NBA prediction markets
notes: Introduce the project in your own words. We study short-horizon activity, not simply which team wins. The original pilot and the later final test are distinct stages.

title: Two questions, with separate forecasting baselines
notes: The reverse task must control for posting persistence. A correlation or post-event rise alone cannot answer either incremental-prediction question.

title: Separate development, extension and replication
notes: Do not call all 66 games held out. Only the final 34 form the last replication test. Earlier stages informed the final design; no test-based hyperparameter search was used.

title: One minute: known features first, future target second
notes: The first extension used an inclusive final-minute flag. That was corrected transparently, with old outputs retained. The correction preceded the November replication. Creation/indexing timestamps have a separate sensitivity check.

title: Attention is measured; news content needs validation
notes: Search coverage succeeded for all collected minutes but is not proof of exhaustive indexing or relevance. AI review suggestions are separate from the blank human-label file. Injury keywords include figurative uses and repeated availability reports.

title: Score the comparison, not just one fitted model
notes: RMSE is not percentage accuracy. Relative RMSE changes are percentages of error, not probability percentage points. Multiple endpoints are reported rather than selecting a favorable specification.

title: The final baseline comparisons have measured gains
notes: Price pooled RMSE: 0.239637 to 0.233446. Volume pooled RMSE: 1.610940 to 1.372064. The old eight-game no-change comparison must not be generalized to this larger final test.

title: Increment from Bluesky: small point estimates, uncertainty
notes: Left: next-minute signed price; right: next-five-minute log volume. Negative is lower error versus the market baseline. The complete social bundle gives −0.073% for price and +0.348% for volume; both game intervals span zero. Counts-only estimates and other horizons remain visible in the workbook. Do not state that no information can ever exist.

title: Reverse direction: market features predicting posting
notes: Reference is posting history plus game state, not a constant forecast. Adding price/trading gives about 0.405% lower five-minute error, but both game/date intervals include zero. Post-event timing is descriptive and does not show that prices caused fans to post.

title: Injury candidates need event-time and source checks
notes: Red marks posting time, not injury onset. Cam Johnson’s ankle injury has team follow-up corroboration, but first publication is unresolved. A scoring play is logged 4.58 seconds after the post. The Walsh limping post lacks independent diagnosis corroboration. Neither demonstrates a news trading edge.

title: Robustness and limitations are part of the evidence
notes: Use the workbook to inspect sensitivity rather than claim a universal result. The final sample spans nine dates. Results can reflect last-trade spread effects and cannot be converted into profit claims.
